_note: Curated 13-pick rotation, one per summer week. APOD does not return future dates via API, so these are hand-selected evergreen kid-friendly entries.

weeks.title: The Pale Blue Dot
weeks.kid: From 4 billion miles away, Voyager 1 turned its camera back at Earth. We're the tiny speck in the sunbeam. Everyone you've ever known has lived right here.

weeks.title: Jupiter's Great Red Spot
weeks.kid: A storm bigger than Earth that has been spinning on Jupiter for at least 350 years. Juno flew right over it and took this picture.

weeks.title: The Sombrero Galaxy
weeks.kid: A galaxy shaped like a Mexican hat, 28 million light-years away. It has 2,000 globular clusters — that's a lot of star families.

weeks.title: Saturn from Cassini
weeks.kid: Cassini flew through Saturn's shadow and took 323 photos to make this picture. Earth is the tiny dot just inside the rings.

weeks.title: Crab Nebula
weeks.kid: The leftovers of a star that exploded in the year 1054. Chinese astronomers saw the explosion in daylight. The nebula is still flying apart.

weeks.title: Earthrise from Apollo 8
weeks.kid: The most famous photo of Earth. Apollo 8 was the first crew to orbit the Moon, and they looked back and saw home rising over the lunar surface.

weeks.title: Pillars of Creation
weeks.kid: Towers of cold gas where new stars are being born, in the Eagle Nebula. The biggest pillar is 4 light-years tall — bigger than the distance to the nearest star.

weeks.title: Mars from Perseverance
weeks.kid: A robot's-eye view of Mars. Perseverance landed in 2021 in an ancient lake bed to look for fossils of microscopic life.

weeks.title: The Milky Way Over Idaho
weeks.credit: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day
weeks.kid: Our home galaxy from a dark-sky site. There are about 100 billion stars in the picture. Most of them have planets. Some of those planets probably have life.

weeks.title: Total Solar Eclipse
weeks.kid: The Moon perfectly covers the Sun. You can only see the Sun's corona — its outer atmosphere — during the few minutes of totality. Idaho was in the path in 2017.

weeks.title: The Andromeda Galaxy
weeks.kid: The closest big galaxy to ours, 2.5 million light-years away. In about 4 billion years it will collide with the Milky Way. They'll merge into one giant galaxy.

weeks.title: Lunar Surface Up Close
weeks.kid: Footprints on the Moon. Apollo 17 was the last time humans walked on another world. The footprints are still there — there's no wind or rain to wash them away.

weeks.title: The Whirlpool Galaxy
weeks.kid: A spiral galaxy eating a smaller galaxy. The smaller one is being pulled apart by gravity. Galaxies do this all the time over billions of years.
